subject: Steam auth-ticket activation, recipient validation and game-server association boundaries
scope: Read-only implementation and public-document research; no account login, ticket creation or game connection performed

observations: createAuthSessionTicket(appid) obtains a legitimate ownership ticket and a Steam-issued game-connect token, builds a session ticket and activates it through ClientAuthList.
New own tickets are cached with estate=0; tickets owned by another user are cached with estate=1.
ClientTicketAuthComplete is matched to an active ticket using ticket_crc.
A non-OK eauth_session_response removes the ticket from the active list.
The event's estate replaces the cached ticket estate.
getActiveAuthSessionTickets reports validated as cached estate > 1.
For an own ticket the completion event is emitted as authTicketStatus; for another user's ticket it is authTicketValidation.
For an own ticket the library comments that the returned SteamID identifies the entity which validated it.
installedSteamUser.interpretation: For a unique own ticket sent only to the current peer, an active validated=true is evidence that the library observed recipient-side ticket completion with an OK response. It does not establish inclusion in a Facepunch player-count batch.
limitations: No official numeric estate enum mapping was found. The initial values and validated comparison above are implementation facts, not official names for all possible states.
validated=false can mean no successful completion was observed by this client. It is not by itself proof of a particular rejection reason.
An active-ticket boolean is not a permanent history of past validations; cancellation, disconnect or an error can remove the ticket.
A generic own-ticket validated flag does not identify a target server without internal ticket/run association. No server or player identity should be exposed just to provide this diagnostic.

distinction: TicketAcceptedCallback handles ClientAuthListAck and is described as Steam accepting the auth ticket as valid.
TicketAuthCompleteCallback handles ClientTicketAuthComplete and is described as a generated ticket having been used to authenticate the user.
Its State is a uint described as Authentication state, with no numeric enum documented there.
Its SteamID property is documented as the game server's SteamID.

officialSdkBoundary.signature: HAuthTicket GetAuthSessionTicket(void *pTicket, int cbMaxTicket, uint32 *pcbTicket, const SteamNetworkingIdentity *pIdentityRemote)
officialSdkBoundary.remoteIdentity: The identity of the remote system authenticating the ticket; a game-server SteamID may be used if obtained from a trusted third party, otherwise use the IP address.
officialSdkBoundary.finding: The current documented SDK supports identifying the intended verifier. The installed node-steam-user createAuthSessionTicket(appid) API has no remote-identity argument.
officialSdkBoundary.limitation: This API difference does not prove a ticket already accepted by a game server must be absent from external player counts. The installed Rust caller still requires separate examination.

officialSdkBoundary.quote: When you are using Steam authentication system this call is never required, the auth system automatically sets the appropriate rich presence.
officialSdkBoundary.finding: There is no documented general requirement to add AdvertiseGame to a correctly completed Steam-authentication session. Reporting the actual connected game address through presence can be an honest experiment, but its necessity for trusted counts has not been established.

officialSdkBoundary.quote: This is part of the old user authentication API and should not be mixed with the new API.
officialSdkBoundary.finding: Do not add the deprecated three-way authentication handshake to an existing GetAuthSessionTicket/BeginAuthSession flow as a speculative fix.
Ticket identity is not confirmed until the receiver gets ValidateAuthTicketResponse_t and checks for success. Returning a ticket to the sender is not the same event.

publicFacepunchWrapper.finding: GetAuthSessionTicket(NetIdentity identity) passes the identity by reference to the native SDK. GetAuthSessionTicketAsync waits for its SDK response before returning.
publicFacepunchWrapper.limitation: Public repository code alone does not prove which identity value an installed Rust build uses.

nextDiagnostic: Observe the current run's own-ticket validation boolean, a strictly matched Steam GMS auth_players response, a changed Facepunch batch timestamp and a manually refreshed browser count. Keep activation, verification and external statistics separate.
privacy: No credentials, tickets, tokens, ticket CRCs, player SteamIDs or private account data are included.
